conclusion: The daemon trace is authoritative for native execution, private signal transition, and post-ACK quarantine; the runtime client is authoritative only for completion and bytes delivered to it. A normal completed disconnect, pre-SUBMIT lease cleanup, and post-ACK in-flight quarantine are distinct outcomes.
decision: Keep wire signal_value_bits=1 and signal_after_observed=false because v2.0 has no wire after-value. Record native private signal 1->0 only in the daemon trace. Accept positive completion only with type 20, three D2H oracles, UNMAP, and session cleanup; accept the negative only when the daemon emits quarantine_cleanup with no type 20/D2H/UNMAP and releases queue, pins, adapter, and owner resources.
invalidated_assumptions: The client negative JSON alone proves remote quarantine cleanup.
The native private 1->0 signal transition is a wire post-signal field.
A normal completed-session EOF is the same as an in-flight post-ACK disconnect.
A daemon output CRC is equivalent to bytes actually delivered to the client without D2H verification.
observation: The positive trace reaches retired, durable type 20, and session complete, then performs ordinary cleanup. The separate disconnect-after-ACK client receives no wait/type 20/D2H/UNMAP, while the daemon emits exactly one quarantine_cleanup record with owner_disconnected=true, owner_quarantined=true, type20_durable=false, native_queue_retired=true, external_pins_released=true, adapter_released=true, and cleanup_complete=true.
question_or_symptom: How are post-ACK disconnect cleanup and completion-signal observations proven without confusing client, wire, and daemon state?
